$description: DPF L0 design token source (EP-UX-SYSTEM, BI-CD81FF7C). W3C DTCG-shaped. This file is the CANONICAL source for the static scales — spacing, radius, elevation, type, motion. Do not hand-edit apps/web/app/tokens.generated.css; run `pnpm --filter web build:design-tokens` instead. SCOPE HONESTY: color VALUES are deliberately not here. The light/dark defaults and every color-mix()-derived value are hand-authored in app/globals.css because DTCG cannot express a media-query-conditional value or a color-mix() derivation, and because runtime branding overrides the --dpf-* custom properties live. What lives here for color is only the alias table under $extensions, which maps Tailwind utility names onto those hand-authored properties.

space.$description: 4-pt progression. Semantic steps rather than a parallel numeric scale — Tailwind's built-in p-1..p-96 already covers raw 4-pt spacing and stays legal. These names give the L1 page shells and L2 budgets a constrained vocabulary to measure against.

lg.$description: Default gap between bands within a shell.

md.$description: Matches the form-control radius already baked into globals.css @layer components.

elevation.$description: Step names are load-bearing: shadow-dpf-{xs,sm,md,lg} are already written across 29 component call sites that silently rendered nothing while the stale v3 tailwind.config.ts defined them and Tailwind v4 never read it. Defining them here is what makes those call sites resolve.

font.$description: The type scale is where visual hierarchy stops being ad-hoc. Six steps with a paired line-height each, so `text-dpf-heading` carries its own leading instead of needing `text-3xl font-bold leading-tight` invented per surface.

motion.$description: Easings become @theme entries (Tailwind v4 has an --ease-* namespace, so ease-dpf-standard is a real utility). Durations deliberately do NOT: v4 exposes no --duration-* namespace, so a --duration-dpf-base @theme entry would generate nothing — the precise dead-token failure this BI removes. Durations are emitted as plain --dpf-duration-* properties, consumable in CSS or as duration-[var(--dpf-duration-base)].

com.dpf.colorAliases.$description: Utility-name -> existing custom property. Generates --color-dpf-* @theme entries so `bg-dpf-accent` / `text-dpf-muted` / `border-dpf-border` exist as real utilities. The VALUE stays var(--dpf-*), so the light defaults, the prefers-color-scheme dark block, and runtime BrandingConfig overrides all keep flowing through untouched. The pre-existing bg-[var(--dpf-*)] arbitrary-value spelling (7,700+ call sites) remains legal and resolves to the identical property.

com.dpf.animations.$description: Keyframe animations are a CSS composition (keyframes + duration + easing), not a DTCG token type, so they live under $extensions rather than being forced into a shape the spec does not define. `duration` and `easing` reference the motion scales above by key. The global prefers-reduced-motion guard in globals.css neutralizes all of these.

com.dpf.density.$description: Density is a CONTEXT, not a utility: the L1 page shells set data-dpf-density on a container and the controls inside read these properties. Emitted as plain custom properties (not @theme) precisely because they are meant to cascade and be overridden per subtree, which @theme entries are not.
